newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 28.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Prime Minister John Major has told his cabinet colleagues that he intends to hold the British general election on May 1.
- The position of loyalist fringe parties at the multi-party talks in Northern Ireland was secured when none of the other participants sought their exclusion.
- U.S. senator George Mitchell has told a U.S. newspaper that chairing the multi-party talks in Northern Ireland is a "labour of love."
- The recent shortage of blood donations in Ireland has caused a number of operations to be cancelled at the Meath Hospital in Dublin.
- The rapid rise of the Irish pound against European currencies is largely the product of speculation on a rise in British interest rates, the Minister for Finance, Ruairi Quinn, said on Monday.
- A full-scale siege was under way in Tallaght, County Dublin, early on Tuesday morning, as a man held a neighbour hostage at knifepoint.
- There was a food hygiene alert on Monday after a child died from complications from an illness caused by the same E Coli bacteria which has recently claimed 19 lives in Scotland.
- Ireland's Finance Minister, Ruairi Quinn, on Monday hit back at "prophets of doom" who warn of trade damage caused by the Irish pound's high exchange value against hardcore EU currencies.
- Dublin's International Financials Services Centre came under attack last night as key EU Finance Ministers demanded an end to "tax havens operating unfair competition."
